title: 4/5 — the rep was polite, but please actually check my account this time before replying. Last time an agent told me the second $89 was just a "temporary authorization, clears in 3 days" and closed the ticket — that was wrong. The money stayed held, and when I called my bank they said it wasn't a normal authorization at all: it was tied to a fraud review already open on my account, case CASE-4471.

This is important — your previous feedback explicitly contradicts the standard "temporary authorization" explanation. Let me check the fraud case you referenced before responding.Here's what I found, and I want to be straightforward with you because your previous feedback matters:

## Current invoice INV-30984
- **TXN-711204** — $89, **settled** (real charge: July Pro subscription)
- **AUTH-711203** — $89, **pending authorization** (flagged as a temporary card authorization, expected to release within 3 business days)

The system's standard assessment is that only one charge has actually settled and no refund is needed.

## Your previous support history (TKT-77106, March 2026)
The same situation: two $89 entries, and the agent gave you the same "temporary authorization, clears in 3 days" explanation. You closed the ticket, but your satisfaction survey made clear that explanation was **wrong** — the hold didn't release, and your bank told you it was tied to fraud case **CASE-4471**.

## My honest assessment
I tried to pull up CASE-4471 to verify whether the current pending $89 is connected to the same fraud review, but I was **not able to retrieve any data on that case** from my end. So I cannot confirm or deny that the current AUTH-711203 is fraud-related the way the previous one was.

Because of that, I don't want to repeat last time's mistake and just tell you "it's a normal authorization, ignore it." But I also can't issue a refund on the settled TXN-711204 without evidence that it was erroneous — that one is a legitimate July Pro subscription charge.

## What I'd recommend
1. **Watch AUTH-711203 closely** — if it has not released within 3 business days, that matches your prior experience and strongly suggests it's not a normal authorization.
2. If it doesn't release, contact your card issuer and ask whether it's tied to an open fraud case on your account.
3. If it is fraud-related, reply to your open ticket **TKT-91842** and let me know — at that point a refund/adjustment would be warranted, and I can escalate to our fraud team with the case reference.
